blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: На ___ (следующий вечер, acc. sg.) Катерина Васильевна еще внимательнее всматривалась в Соловцова.
exercises.why: **вечер → вечер** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **следующий → следующий** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with вечер). Adjective type IV, sibilant (after ж, ч, ш, щ) — declines like DLI's хороший (every form has the same endings): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. вечер · вечера · вечеру · вечер · вечером · вечере; pl. вечера · вечеров · вечерам · вечера · вечерами · вечерах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Всего ___ (час, acc. sg.) назад, часу нет.
exercises.why: **час → час** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). Declension: sg. час · часа · часу · час · часом · часе; pl. часы · часов · часам · часы · часами · часах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Если бы все это в ___ (тёмная ночь, acc. sg.) залить огнем?
exercises.why: **ночь → ночь** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's часть — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. часть). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **тёмный → темную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with ночь). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings): A. новую. Ending -ая → -ую.  Declension: sg. ночь · ночи · ночи · ночь · ночью · ночи; pl. ночи · ночей · ночам · ночи · ночами · ночах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Самого Неручева и след простыл на ___ (этот день, acc. sg.) в собрании.
exercises.why: **день → день** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's автомобиль — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. автомобиль). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **этот → этот** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with день). «этот» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (m. sg.): этот · этого · этому · этот (inan.) / этого (anim.) · этим · этом.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Вот что произошло в ___ (голубой день, acc. sg.) июньский.
exercises.why: **день → день** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's автомобиль — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. автомобиль). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **голубой → голубой** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with день). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ый): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (тот год, acc. pl.) в Технологическом институте было много студентов-варшавян.
exercises.why: **год → годы** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural годы. Declines like DLI's стол — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. столы). Ending — (no ending) → -ы.  **тот → те** (acc. pl., agreeing with годы). «тот» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (pl.): те · тех · тем · те (inan.) / тех (anim.) · теми · тех.  Declension: sg. год · года · году · год · годом · годе; pl. годы · годов · годам · годы · годами · годах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Письмо насчет приезда одних людей на ___ (праздник, acc. pl.).
exercises.why: **праздник → праздники** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural праздники. Declines like DLI's стол — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. столы). Ending — (no ending) → -и.  Declension: sg. праздник · праздника · празднику · праздник · праздником · празднике; pl. праздники · праздников · праздникам · праздники · праздниками · праздниках.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «The letter ы never follows г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ; therefore: книга — книги, река — реки, госпожа — госпожи.» — DLI, Lesson 23.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (нерабочий день, acc. pl.) с нашим удовольствием!
exercises.why: **день → дни** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural дни. Declines like DLI's автомобиль — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. автомобили). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.
